svg.title: FROST CPU and X3 memory architecture
svg.desc: RV64GCBV out-of-order CPU with a VLEN 256 vector unit. IF, PD and ID feed a four-bundle decoded queue, two-wide dispatch and INT/FP register renaming with twelve branch checkpoints and a speculative vtype tracker. Branch prediction combines a 256-entry BTB, a 1024-entry two-way backing BTB, a 1024-entry bimodal predictor, a four-table 4 x 1024 tagged direction predictor, a three-table 3 x 256 indirect target predictor and an 8-entry return address stack. Dispatch allocates the 32-entry reorder buffer, four reservation stations, memory queues and the four-entry vector memory table. The INT, MUL, FP and MEM stations have 16, 4, 6 and 8 entries. INT issues to two ALUs with branch and JALR resolution on pipe 0. MUL serves integer multiply, divide, carry-less multiply and vector configuration (vset*). FP uses a seven-stage FMA pipeline for add, subtract, multiply and FMA, a radix-16 divider and an FP engine for square root, conversions and misc operations. Two CDB lanes broadcast results across eight FU slots to the reservation stations and ROB; staged loads and the FP pipeline also wake dependents early. The ROB commits up to two instructions in order to INT/FP register files, releases stores, and enqueues committed vector arithmetic into the vector unit's eight-entry issue window (VIQ). CSR accesses execute at commit; traps support M/S/U delegation and vector CSRs. Conditional branch and JALR mispredictions redirect fetch and restore the RAT the cycle after resolution, then flush younger backend work the following cycle. JAL mispredictions and traps recover at commit. A hardware misaligned-access engine assists plain misaligned cached DDR loads and stores at commit. The VLEN 256 vector unit contains vector control (vtype tracking, dispatch legality, per-ROB-tag state and ROB-head VTOX/VTOF completion on CDB slot 6), an eight-entry post-commit issue window (VIQ), the vector engine (32 x 256-bit 5R/2W vector register file, four 64-bit integer lanes, an integer execution unit, a floating-point unit for FP16/32/64 and Zvfh, and a crypto unit for Zvbc/Zvkng AES, SHA-2, GHASH and CLMUL), the four-entry vector memory table (VMT) with head translation and ordering range holds checked by the load and store queues, and the vector memory unit (VMU) with six 32-byte sector slots supporting unit-stride, whole-register, mask, strided, indexed and segment operations over an eight-ID coherent hart line client shared with the misaligned-access engine. Sv39 uses a 16-entry ITLB in IF, a 16-entry DTLB ahead of the eight-entry load and store queues, a shared 512-entry four-way L2 TLB with a 32-entry superpage side array, and one shared page-table walker with a pointer walk cache. The load queue contains a direct-mapped 512-entry, eight-byte-granule L0 cache and receives store forwarding. Matching I, D and V badges connect the CPU to the system view below. Cached instruction fetch uses a two-active, six-victim fetch buffer and 16 KiB L1I with two miss slots; cached data uses a 128 KiB MSI L1D with eight read slots, eight request endpoints (seven available for ordinary load misses, two supporting stream prefetch), four ordered store records and a Zicbom CMO requester. A read-hit pipeline serves eligible loads beside miss, store, grant and probe service. The shared walker's ReadOncePTW requests and instruction ReadOnceIF refills reach the L2 home, which probes L1D and merges dirty data. Coherent ingress joins the 256-bit AXI4 DMA mux (NIC, DMA test engine and Svpbmt uncached DDR alias, eight slots) and the eight-ID hart line client (VMU and misaligned-access engine); the home orders them through L1D probes, dirty-data merges and load-queue cuts. Tagged channels join L1D, IF, PTW, VMU/MA, CMO, DMA and prefetch requests at the 2 MiB UltraRAM L2 home (four-way, 64-byte lines, eight fills). A coherent prefetch agent tracks four data and two instruction streams (three data and one instruction request in flight) and fills the L2. Private sectors are 32 bytes and home lines are 64 bytes; all three DDR caches are four-way. A 512-bit AXI4 master reaches the board DDR4 controller for a 1 GiB cached region at 0x80000000, and also serves 256 KiB low BRAM (with an 8 KiB instruction cache, L0 data reads and write-through stores) and SoC MMIO. SoC devices include UART, FIFO0/1, CLINT, a five-source APLIC with direct and MSI delivery to the CPU's M/S IMSIC files, the memory error unit, SYSRESET, and the NIC and DMA engine's 64-bit AXI4-Lite registers. JTAG connects through the DTM to the debug module for halt, resume and single-step. Capacities show the X3 configuration. Only selected connections are drawn; memory arrows follow requests, with responses omitted.
